sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether a state can impose jail time without providing a lawyer. The defendant argues this practice violates the Sixth Amendment. The state argues it can use fines as a substitute for counsel.

sections.heading: What each side wants

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Alabama argues the Sixth Amendment does not require a lawyer if the defendant pays fines.
Shelton argues the Sixth Amendment requires a lawyer for any criminal prosecution that risks jail.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Does the Sixth Amendment require a lawyer for a misdemeanor that carries a jail sentence?
Can a state use a fine as a substitute for providing a lawyer?

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of the right to counsel. It determines when states must provide lawyers for criminal defendants. It affects how courts handle misdemeanor prosecutions nationwide.
